name: Coolify

auth.keyHelp: In your Coolify open Keys & Tokens > API Tokens, create a token with only the read permission, and copy it at once; it is shown once.

notes: Coolify runs on the user own host, so every URL uses {site}. Base URL is https://<your-coolify-domain>/api/v1 (Coolify Cloud is https://app.coolify.io/api/v1). Auth is Authorization: Bearer <token>; the token is shown as ID|secret and the whole value must be sent. Request JSON with Accept: application/json. The key page depends on the user host: the docs only say open Keys & Tokens in the sidebar, then API Tokens, and give no URL path, so keyUrl is just {site}. Read-only is possible: token permissions are read (list and inspect, sensitive values stay redacted), read:sensitive (secrets, logs, env values; also adds read), write, deploy (deploy, restart, stop, cancel; a deploy-only token) and root (bypasses every check). Use only read. Only team admins and owners can use tokens with read:sensitive, write, deploy or root; a plain team member can use only read tokens. A token is bound to the team that was active when it was created and cannot see another team. Self-hosted gate: an instance admin must set API access to Enabled under Settings > Advanced (API and MCP section); with it off, even a valid token gets 403; the optional Allowed API IPs list applies to every call, so the Hub host IP may need adding. Tokens can expire (7, 30, 60, 90 days, 1 year or never). Test call: GET /version needs only a valid token and returns the Coolify version as plain text, so who is null. The docs examples show GET /api/v1/teams/current for a first call, but the endpoint reference lists the team call as GET /team (Authenticated Team, returns id, name, description and members), so the two pages disagree and I did not use either as the test; if /team works it would be a better who source. Which permission GET /version needs is not stated beyond Bearer auth. POST /deploy takes uuid and tag as query parameters (comma separated lists accepted) plus force; it needs the deploy permission, so a read-only token cannot use it and the write action will fail, which is intended. GET /deployments lists only currently running deployments. Official MCP: Coolify has its own built-in MCP server on every instance at {site}/mcp, Streamable HTTP, authenticated with the same Bearer API token (no OAuth). On self-hosted it is off by default and returns 404 until an admin sets MCP server to Enabled in Settings > Advanced, and MCP must also be enabled for the team; MCP shows only the tools the token permissions allow. The docs call for a public HTTPS URL. Verify with get_current_team or get_infrastructure_overview. Deploy (POST /deploy) is left out on purpose: the Hub offers no deploy action on this service for now.
